candidate.answerReason: Exhausting all distinct eligible prime pairs shows that 119 is the only listed result. It is obtained from 11 and 13.

methods.label: Check the distinct prime pairs systematically
methods.explanation:
The primes between \(4\) and \(18\) are \(5,7,11,13,17\). Write the chosen pair as \(p<q\). This lists each pair once because reversing the two primes does not change their sum or product.

For each smaller prime \(p\), use every larger prime from the list in increasing order. The resulting values of \(pq-(p+q)\) are
\[
\begin{aligned}
p=5 &: \quad 23,39,47,63,\\
p=7 &: \quad 59,71,95,\\
p=11 &: \quad 119,159,\\
p=13 &: \quad 191.
\end{aligned}
\]
These cases exhaust all distinct pairs. Only \(119\) appears among the choices; specifically,
\[
11\cdot13-(11+13)=143-24=\boxed{119}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
